caption: The video captures a tabletop physics demonstration held in a fixed view. On the left, an open spiral notepad displays the handwritten equation n = C/V with small explanatory text beneath it. On the right, a clear drinking glass partly filled with water holds a yellow pencil set at a diagonal angle. The submerged portion of the pencil appears displaced and bent relative to the segment above the waterline, an optical effect that persists unchanged across the entire excerpt. Behind the table, a person in a black shirt stands motionless, a thin white cable hanging down in front of them. A whiteboard is mounted on the wall to the right of the glass, and the camera framing stays constant, with no pan, tilt, or zoom detectable across the frames. No object, person, or prop changes location during the clip, so the refraction demonstration remains on display in its ongoing state throughout the visible portion.
